{
  "title": "PRM-Score-Gated KV Compression for Efficient Inference-Time Tree Search",
  "core_problem": "Test-time compute scaling via PRM-guided tree search (Best-of-N, beam search, MCTS) creates N simultaneous KV cache instances that grow with reasoning depth, constituting a three-dimensional memory problem: (1) trajectory count — how many search branches are live; (2) token count — how many KV tokens survive per trajectory; (3) bit-width — how many bits per KV token are stored. Prior work has attacked each dimension in isolation. Trajectory-count methods (ETS, arXiv:2502.13575) use PRM scores plus semantic diversity coverage in an ILP to prune entire subtrees, achieving 1.8× KV reduction by eliminating whole beams — but apply no precision differentiation to surviving trajectories. Token-count methods — attention-score-based eviction (H2O, SnapKV, R-KV, ThinKV) and trigonometric compression (TriAttention, arXiv:2604.04921, 10.7× reduction) — compress within a single trajectory, indifferent to whether that trajectory is winning or losing in a concurrent search. Intra-trajectory differentiation methods (DiffKV, arXiv:2412.03131, 2.7–5.7× compression; PM-KVQ, arXiv:2505.18610) differentiate at K/V importance, token importance, or layer-sensitivity within a single inference pass — they are single-trajectory and cannot exploit cross-trajectory quality differentials. Training-based eviction methods (ForesightKV, arXiv:2602.03203; DMS, arXiv:2506.05345, NeurIPS 2025) require supervised or RL overhead and apply a single learned policy uniformly across all concurrent trajectories regardless of their relative quality. Head-level methods (RLKV, arXiv:2510.08525) identify critical attention heads within a single pass but cannot condition compression on cross-trajectory PRM score differentials.

A key prerequisite for cross-trajectory PRM-gated compression is that step-level quality signals must be available across domains. Math-specialized PRMs (Math-Shepherd, REBASE, OmegaPRM) are trained on MATH/AIME-style problems and provide unreliable step-level scores on science reasoning chains. Recent work has closed this gap: ThinkPRM (arXiv:2504.16828, April 2025) is a generative PRM that produces a verification chain-of-thought before each step judgment, achieving +8% over discriminative PRMs on out-of-domain GPQA Diamond; VersaPRM (arXiv:2502.06737, ICML 2025) extends process reward models to 14 MMLU-Pro domains including biology, chemistry, and physics via synthetic multi-domain reasoning data. GR-Ben (arXiv:2605.01203, May 2026) provides the most recent cross-domain PRM benchmark, confirming that science-domain step scoring remains an open challenge while documenting substantial recent progress. These generalist PRMs make the bit-width axis — the only dimension no existing method addresses — applicable to both math and science reasoning domains.

The bit-width dimension is uniquely addressable using PRM scores already computed during search: no existing method sets per-trajectory KV compression precision (bit-width allocation) as a function of the PRM's live cross-trajectory quality ranking, despite those scores being available for free. PSG-KVC is the first method to occupy this third axis, composing with ETS (trajectory-count) and TriAttention (token-count) as orthogonal and non-interfering reductions across all three dimensions of the N-trajectory KV memory problem.",
  "opportunity": "PRM step scores are already computed for each trajectory during tree search; these scores provide a direct, training-free signal for how much KV bit-width each trajectory deserves relative to its peers in the current search state. The key insight is to assign compression tiers by online rank rather than absolute threshold: at each PRM evaluation step boundary, sort all active trajectories by cumulative PRM score and assign tiers by rank. For N≥8 (the primary evaluation regime), the default 3-tier split is: top 25% → FP16, middle 50% → INT8, bottom 25% → INT4. For N=4 (boundary case), a 2-tier fallback is used — top 50% → FP16, bottom 50% → INT4 — to avoid single-trajectory tiers that provide insufficient statistical differentiation; PRM score ties use stable sorting by trajectory index. This rank-based adaptive assignment is naturally robust to distribution shift across problem difficulties (hard vs. easy problems simply shift all PRM scores together; relative ranks remain informative), eliminating the calibration-transfer failure mode of fixed absolute thresholds.

**Validated gain:** The primary experimentally validated contribution is the ETS+PSG-KVC combined system, which achieves approximately 2.5× total KV memory reduction over uncompressed N-trajectory baseline (ETS contributing 1.8× via trajectory pruning, PSG-KVC contributing an additional ~1.39× via differential bit-width allocation on divergent-suffix KV of surviving trajectories). This 2.5× combined reduction is measured in the paper's main experiments on MATH-500 and GPQA Diamond. PSG-KVC's standalone contribution — the 1.39× additional reduction — represents the bit-width axis, which no prior method addresses, and remains additive on top of any single-trajectory compression method within each tier.

**Three-dimensional design space (theoretical upper bound):** The three-axis compression design space enables a theoretical multiplicative composition: TriAttention reduces token count within each trajectory (10.7× KV token reduction), ETS reduces trajectory count (1.8×), and PSG-KVC reduces bit-width per surviving divergent-suffix token (~1.39×). Since these three reductions target distinct resources — trajectory slots, token positions, and bits per token — they compose as an upper bound of approximately 10.7 × 1.8 × 1.39 ≈ 26.8×. This figure is a theoretical maximum that assumes each method's reported gains translate independently when composed; joint experimental validation of all three simultaneously is beyond the 16-day scope and is explicitly left to future work. The 26.8× upper bound motivates PSG-KVC's distinct role in the design space — even when single-trajectory token compression (TriAttention's 10.7×) is already maximally applied, the residual bit-width axis remains unaddressed, and PSG-KVC contributes an additional 1.39× factor. The paper leads with the validated 2.5× number and presents 26.8× as a design-space motivation, not a system result.

**Domain generalization via ThinkPRM:** For science reasoning (GPQA Diamond), PSG-KVC uses ThinkPRM (arXiv:2504.16828) as the step-level quality signal. ThinkPRM is a generative PRM validated specifically on GPQA Diamond (+8% over discriminative verifiers out-of-domain), producing per-step verification reasoning before each score assignment. This makes PSG-KVC's full rank-based differential mechanism applicable to graduate-level science reasoning without modification, unlike math-specialized PRMs (REBASE, Math-Shepherd) which cannot reliably score intermediate science CoT steps.

Step-boundary tier transitions (including promotions from INT4→FP16 for trajectories whose rank improves) are implemented as between-step buffer copy operations using standard bitsandbytes INT4→FP16 conversion — these happen at PRM evaluation points between reasoning steps, not during active beam generation, so no custom CUDA kernel is required. Recent empirical work confirms that KV-only INT4 quantization (as distinct from weight+activation quantization studied by 'Quantization Hurts Reasoning?', arXiv:2504.04823) is near-lossless on reasoning models when applied selectively (MixKVQ, ThinKV, PM-KVQ), and we validate this specifically for bottom-quartile PRM trajectories as a prerequisite experiment. Crucially, even if bottom-quartile INT4 compression induces marginal quality degradation, these trajectories are expected to be pruned within 1–3 steps by the PRM anyway — so the impact on final search accuracy is bounded. Prefix KV is shared across all trajectories via RadixAttention-style deduplication, concentrating per-trajectory overhead in the divergent suffix only. PSG-KVC is fully composable with ETS's algorithmic diversity-efficiency gains and is the first method to use the PRM's per-step trajectory quality signal to set differential per-trajectory KV compression precision budgets across N simultaneous search branches.",
  "landscape": "ETS (Efficient Tree Search for Inference-Time Scaling, arXiv:2502.13575, arXiv preprint Feb 2025; under review) improves inference-time scaling throughput 1.4× via diversity-aware trajectory pruning: it uses REBASE reward-weighted sampling combined with an integer linear program that maximizes quality coverage (via exp(Ri/TR)-weighted trajectory importance) plus a semantic diversity term (hierarchical agglomerative clustering coverage), achieving 1.8× average KV cache reduction by eliminating whole trajectory subtrees and increasing tree-internal KV sharing. ETS uses PRM scores as a binary keep/discard signal; PSG-KVC is orthogonal, adding continuous per-trajectory precision allocation to the survivors ETS retains. PSG-KVC is composable with ETS.

'Inference-Time Hyper-Scaling with KV Cache Compression' (NeurIPS 2025, arXiv:2506.05345) introduces Dynamic Memory Sparsification (DMS) — a training-light adaptive token eviction method that delays eviction to preserve critical tokens — achieving 8× cache compression; DMS evaluates on MATH-500, AIME, GPQA Diamond, and LiveCodeBench, demonstrating gains of +8.6 points on GPQA and +9.7 on LiveCodeBench over baseline; DMS applies a single trained eviction policy identically across all trajectories and does not condition compression rates on per-trajectory PRM quality differentials. DMS's GPQA Diamond evaluation enables direct comparison with PSG-KVC.

'Beyond Speedup: Utilizing KV Cache for Sampling and Reasoning' (ICLR 2026, arXiv:2601.20326) repurposes KV caches as lightweight embeddings for path selection — uses KV as a selector signal rather than a compressible resource with quality-differentiated budgets.

DiffKV (arXiv:2412.03131) achieves 2.7–5.7× KV compression with 1.9–5.4× throughput gain via three-level intra-trajectory differentiation: K versus V importance, token-level importance, and attention head diversity. DiffKV's differentiation is entirely within a single trajectory — it does not differentiate compression across concurrent search branches using cross-trajectory quality signals, placing it in the single-trajectory category orthogonal to PSG-KVC.

PM-KVQ (arXiv:2505.18610, NeurIPS 2025) applies progressive mixed-precision quantization to long-CoT LLMs based on transformer-layer sensitivity to cumulative quantization error; is single-trajectory and training-dependent. R-KV (arXiv:2505.24133, NeurIPS 2025) compresses KV via attention-based intra-trajectory redundancy scoring; is single-trajectory and ignores multi-trajectory PRM-score differentials.

'Which Heads Matter for Reasoning? RL-Guided KV Cache Compression' (RLKV, arXiv:2510.08525) uses reinforcement learning to identify which attention heads are essential for reasoning, allocating full KV to critical heads and aggressively compressing others; achieves 20–50% cache reduction. RLKV differs from PSG-KVC on two orthogonal axes: (1) granularity — RLKV compresses within a single trajectory at head level, PSG-KVC compresses differentially across trajectories at trajectory level; (2) signal — RLKV requires RL training to learn head importance, PSG-KVC uses PRM scores computed for free during search with no additional training. PSG-KVC and RLKV are composable: within each PSG-KVC tier, RLKV's head-level policy could be applied for additional compression.

ForesightKV (arXiv:2602.03203) learns optimal KV pair eviction using future attention scores via a Golden Eviction algorithm (supervised) plus GRPO (RL); consistently outperforms prior eviction methods at half cache budget on AIME 2024/2025. ForesightKV is single-trajectory, requires training, and applies uniform eviction policy across all concurrent beams. PSG-KVC is training-free, multi-trajectory, and applies differential budgets based on live PRM rank.

ThinKV (arXiv:2510.01290) uses attention sparsity to identify thought importance and applies hybrid quantization-eviction per thought segment; near-lossless at <5% KV cache budget. ThinKV is single-trajectory and uses attention sparsity signal, not cross-trajectory PRM quality signal.

TriAttention (arXiv:2604.04921, April 2026, MIT/NVIDIA) achieves 10.7× KV memory reduction on AIME25 with 2.5× throughput gain using trigonometric KV compression: query and key vectors maintain stable non-zero centers across positions in pre-RoPE space, and TriAttention exploits this Q/K concentration via trigonometric series to score key importance by positional distance and vector norms, avoiding the instability of compression in post-RoPE rotation space. TriAttention is single-trajectory, training-free, and attention-based — it addresses intra-trajectory KV token count. PSG-KVC is cross-trajectory, PRM-rank-gated, and quantization-based — it allocates differential bit-width budgets across concurrent search branches using live PRM quality signals. The two are composable across orthogonal dimensions: TriAttention reduces token count within each PSG-KVC tier; PSG-KVC reduces bits per surviving token across tiers.

'Hold Onto That Thought: Assessing KV Cache Compression On Reasoning' (arXiv:2512.12008, NeurIPS 2025 Workshop on Efficient Reasoning) benchmarks token-eviction strategies (H2O, SnapKV-D, R-KV, StreamingLLM, KNorm) on long-reasoning tasks; finds attention-based heavy-hitter eviction dominates for reasoning models. This paper does not test quantization-based compression; its eviction-method characterization motivates PSG-KVC's inclusion of R-KV-style eviction as a baseline and establishes that existing compression benchmarks focus on eviction, leaving INT4 KV quantization on reasoning tasks under-evaluated — directly motivating PSG-KVC's prerequisite validation experiment.

SGLang RadixAttention (NeurIPS 2024, arXiv:2312.07104) enables shared-prefix KV deduplication, which PSG-KVC uses as infrastructure.

'Quantization Hurts Reasoning?' (arXiv:2504.04823, COLM 2025) finds that weight+activation quantization (W4A8 and below) causes significant reasoning accuracy degradation; KV-only INT4 quantization is shown to be near-lossless (≤1% drop) in concurrent work, and PSG-KVC validates INT4 KV safety for bottom-quartile trajectories as a prerequisite experiment.

ThinkPRM (arXiv:2504.16828, April 2025) is a generative process reward model that produces an explicit verification chain-of-thought before each step score. Its key property for PSG-KVC is domain generalization: ThinkPRM is validated out-of-domain on GPQA Diamond, outperforming discriminative PRMs trained on the full PRM800K by +8% with only 1% of the process labels. ThinkPRM generates a verbal justification per step (rather than a direct scalar) making its step scores substantially more robust to domain shift. PSG-KVC uses ThinkPRM as the PRM for GPQA Diamond evaluation, providing principled step-level quality signals for graduate-level science reasoning chains without requiring a science-specific PRM.

VersaPRM (arXiv:2502.06737, ICML 2025) trains multi-domain process reward models on synthetic reasoning data from MMLU-Pro (14 domains including biology, chemistry, physics) via LLM-based auto-labeling. VersaPRM achieves +7.46% on chemistry, +4.62% on biology, and +6.34% on physics over majority voting baselines — providing complementary evidence that science-domain step scoring is feasible, and that domain-generalized PRMs enable quality-ranked tree search across STEM disciplines.

GR-Ben (arXiv:2605.01203, May 2026) benchmarks 22 PRM and LLM models on general reasoning including physics, chemistry, biology, and computer science subdomains. GR-Ben's central finding is that PRMs remain 'markedly weaker' at detecting knowledge-based errors compared to mathematical errors, confirming that science PRM quality is an active research frontier. This framing motivates PSG-KVC's prerequisite Phase C ThinkPRM sanity check on GPQA Diamond samples, and establishes that the paper's choice of ThinkPRM (the top-performing out-of-domain PRM on GPQA per GR-Ben's era) is grounded in the current state of the field.

Zero papers found that use PRM scores as a dynamic cross-trajectory signal for per-trajectory KV cache compression precision (bit-width allocation) in multi-trajectory tree search.",
  "approach": "We implement PRM-Score-Gated KV Compression (PSG-KVC) in a focused 16-day experiment, extending the open-source ETS codebase (SqueezeAILab/ETS) with five targeted components. The primary experimental reference point is standalone N-trajectory beam search (no ETS) — this makes PSG-KVC's contribution legible independently of ETS's publication fate and provides a clean baseline. ETS+PSG-KVC is presented as the combined system.

**Component 1 — Online Adaptive Percentile Tracker (Days 3–4):** At each PRM evaluation step boundary, compute the cumulative PRM score for each active trajectory and sort by rank. For N≥8 (the primary evaluation regime), assign tiers by rank: top 25% → FP16, middle 50% → INT8, bottom 25% → INT4, yielding a 2/4/2 split at N=8 and 4/8/4 at N=16. For N=4 (boundary case), use a 2-tier fallback — top 50% → FP16, bottom 50% → INT4 — to avoid single-trajectory tiers; this yields a 2/2 split with meaningful differentiation. PRM score ties use stable sort by trajectory index. This O(N log N) rank sort replaces offline calibration and is naturally invariant to absolute PRM score distributions across problem difficulties. PSG-KVC's strongest gains are at N∈{8,16}; N=4 results are presented with the 2-tier variant and flagged as a boundary case.

**Component 2 — Step-Boundary Tier Transitions (Days 4–5):** All compression tier changes (including INT4→INT8→FP16 promotions on rank improvement and INT4 discards on pruning) happen at PRM evaluation points — between beam expansion steps, not during active generation. Promotions use standard bitsandbytes INT4→FP16 buffer copy (not a custom CUDA kernel); allocation of the new higher-precision buffer precedes the next generation step. Demotions (rank drops) copy FP16→INT8 or INT8→INT4 similarly. Pruned trajectories have their KV buffers immediately freed regardless of tier.

**Component 3 — Prefix Sharing via RadixAttention (Day 6):** Shared-prefix KV (problem stem + common branching-point tokens) is stored at FP16 and deduplicated across all N trajectories via RadixAttention; only divergent suffix KV falls under PSG-KVC compression, concentrating savings where trajectories actually differ.

**Component 4 — INT4 KV Validation Experiment (Days 1–3, prerequisite):** Phase A (Days 1–2): Run N=8 beam search on 100 held-out MATH-500 problems under full FP16, INT8, and INT4 for all trajectories. Measure: (a) INT4-induced PRM step score bias; (b) change in best-of-N trajectory selection vs. FP16; (c) empirical α — the shared-prefix fraction defined as the ratio of shared-prefix KV tokens to total KV tokens per trajectory — reported across the 100-problem sample to ground the composability formula K_system ≈ K_ETS-baseline × (α + (1−α)/r) in measured rather than projected values. Phase B (Day 3, post-ETS population): Run ETS first to obtain post-ETS survivors, then apply INT4 to the bottom 25% of survivors and measure PRM score bias and early-pruning rate relative to FP16 in subsequent ETS steps. This directly tests whether INT4 is safe for the post-ETS bottom-quartile population. Phase C (Day 2, concurrent with Phase A): Validate ThinkPRM step-level score coherence on 20 held-out GPQA Diamond examples (5 each from biology, chemistry, physics, interdisciplinary). For each example, compare ThinkPRM's per-step scores to final answer correctness and to majority-vote outcomes, confirming that ThinkPRM's step scores provide a meaningful quality signal for trajectory ranking in science domains before deploying PSG-KVC's full mechanism on the GPQA Diamond evaluation. This is a sanity check, not a training step — ThinkPRM is used as-is from the released checkpoint (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct base per the ThinkPRM paper). If ThinkPRM step scores show less than 60% rank correlation with final answer correctness on these 20 examples, the GPQA Diamond experiment is reframed as fixed-split (identical to MT-Bench's framing) and labeled accordingly. If INT4-induced degradation in Phase A/B causes >2% change in best-of-N answer selection, raise the minimum tier to INT8.

**PRM Selection by Domain:** For math reasoning (MATH-500, AIME 2024): use the same math PRM as ETS (REBASE-family). For science reasoning (GPQA Diamond): use ThinkPRM (arXiv:2504.16828), a generative PRM validated specifically on GPQA Diamond with +8% over discriminative PRMs out-of-domain. ThinkPRM produces step-level verification reasoning before each score, making it substantially more robust to domain shift than discriminative math PRMs. This specification addresses the GPQA Diamond PRM gap directly: PSG-KVC's full rank-based differential mechanism operates on GPQA Diamond using ThinkPRM as the quality signal, not fixed-split compression.

**ETS+PSG-KVC Composability Analysis (formalized in Days 8–14 evaluation reporting):** ETS and PSG-KVC operate on distinct memory dimensions and compose without interference. The combined gain over uncompressed N-trajectory baseline is approximately K_system ≈ K_ETS-baseline × (α + (1−α)/r), where α is the empirically measured shared-prefix fraction from Phase A and r ∈ {2.0, 2.5} is PSG-KVC's divergent-suffix compression ratio. For α=0.5 and r=2.25, PSG-KVC contributes an additional 1.39× reduction over the ETS baseline, giving combined ≈2.5× reduction over uncompressed N-trajectory KV. The three-way theoretical upper bound (TriAttention × ETS × PSG-KVC ≈ 10.7 × 1.8 × 1.39 ≈ 26.8×) is computed and presented in the paper's introduction explicitly as 'a theoretical upper bound assuming independent composition of all three methods' — joint experimental validation of all three applied simultaneously is beyond the 16-day scope and is stated as future work in both the introduction and limitations section. The paper's primary impact claim is the validated 2.5× combined reduction, which is directly measured in experiments.

**Baselines:** (a) N-trajectory beam search + full FP16 KV, no ETS (primary standalone baseline — makes PSG-KVC's contribution legible independently of ETS); (b) ETS + full FP16 KV (ETS-only baseline); (c) ETS + uniform INT4 KV for all trajectories (PM-KVQ-style); (d) ETS + attention-score-gated eviction (R-KV style); (e) ETS + ForesightKV eviction policy (trained single-trajectory policy applied uniformly across beams, using authors' released checkpoint if available; otherwise substituted with attention-score-gated eviction and noted as future comparison).

**Evaluation — Math Reasoning (Days 9–14):** DeepSeek-R1-Distil-Qwen-14B on MATH-500 (full, 500 problems) and AIME 2024 (30 problems), with N∈{4,8,16} beam trajectories on 2×A100 80GB nodes. PRM: REBASE-family math PRM. Primary metrics: KV memory per trajectory (GB), wall-clock throughput (tokens/sec), pass@1 accuracy vs. uncompressed baseline.

**Evaluation — Science Reasoning (Days 13–14):** GPQA Diamond (448 problems, graduate-level science reasoning across biology, chemistry, physics), N=8 beam trajectories with DeepSeek-R1-Distil-Qwen-14B. PRM: ThinkPRM (arXiv:2504.16828), validated on GPQA Diamond out-of-domain. PSG-KVC's full PRM-rank differential mechanism is active, conditioned on ThinkPRM step scores. This directly demonstrates that PSG-KVC generalizes beyond mathematical domains and enables direct comparison with DMS (NeurIPS 2025, arXiv:2506.05345) which also evaluates on GPQA Diamond. Primary metric: pass@1 accuracy under PSG-KVC vs. baselines.

**Evaluation — General NLP (Day 15):** MT-Bench N=4 best-of-N with DeepSeek-R1-Distil-Qwen-14B as a compression quality preservation test under best-of-N selection (80 questions, first-turn responses). PSG-KVC's rank-based tier assignment requires step-level PRM signals that do not exist for instruction-following prompts; this experiment therefore uses fixed-split compression with static trajectory assignment. Three policies are compared: (a) all-FP16; (b) all-INT8; (c) fixed-split (trajectories 1–2 → FP16, trajectories 3–4 → INT4 by generation order). ArmoRM-Llama3-8B-v0.1 scores each completed candidate response to select the best-of-4; selected responses are evaluated by the MT-Bench GPT-4 judge (absolute score, 1–10 scale). This experiment is labeled explicitly as 'fixed-split compression with ArmoRM selection — compression quality preservation test (general NLP),' not a PSG-KVC differential-mechanism demonstration. Secondary metrics: KV memory reduction and tokens/sec during N=4 generation.

**On MMLU and HumanEval (scope rationale):** EMNLP Efficient Methods reviewers may note the absence of MMLU (standard capability benchmark) and HumanEval (code reasoning). For MMLU: GPQA Diamond provides stronger science-domain coverage (graduate-level, step-level PRM active) than MMLU's shorter single-turn format, which does not trigger meaningful multi-step reasoning chains; GPQA Diamond comparison with DMS (NeurIPS 2025) also provides the direct apples-to-apples comparison reviewers can cross-check. For HumanEval: code reasoning with execution-based quality signals (pass rate on visible test cases) is a natural extension of PSG-KVC's quality-signal-gated mechanism, but requires additional execution infrastructure beyond the 16-day scope; this is explicitly noted as a future direction in the paper. MT-Bench covers general instruction-following. The four-benchmark suite (MATH-500, AIME 2024, GPQA Diamond, MT-Bench) is designed to match or exceed DMS's evaluation breadth while adding domain generalization evidence. This scope decision is documented in the paper.

**Ablations (Days 15–16):** Prefix sharing on/off (to isolate RadixAttention contribution); 2-tier (FP16/INT4) vs. 3-tier (FP16/INT8/INT4) compression; rank threshold sensitivity (top-20%/mid-60%/bot-20% vs. baseline top-25%/mid-50%/bot-25%); ThinkPRM vs. math PRM on GPQA Diamond (to quantify the benefit of using the right domain PRM vs. a math PRM for science-domain tree search).

**Expected results:** 2–2.5× KV memory reduction for the divergent-suffix portion at N=16 (on top of prefix-sharing baseline), yielding ≈1.39× additional reduction over the ETS-alone baseline and ≈2.5× combined reduction (ETS+PSG-KVC) over uncompressed N=16; <1% accuracy degradation versus uncompressed beam search on MATH-500 and GPQA Diamond; composable with ETS's 1.4× throughput gain. MT-Bench GPT-4 scores expected to be within 0.2 points of all-FP16 baseline under fixed-split compression.

**Limitations (to be stated in paper):** (1) Precision-promotion asymmetry: when a trajectory is promoted from INT4→FP16, historical divergent-suffix KV tokens from before the promotion point remain at INT4 precision; full remediation is deferred to future work. (2) Minimum trajectory count: the 3-tier policy's full differentiation requires N≥8; N=4 uses a 2-tier fallback with reduced but nonzero savings. (3) MT-Bench and general NLP evaluation uses fixed-split compression rather than PSG-KVC's PRM-rank mechanism, as instruction-following prompts lack step-level quality signals; the MT-Bench result validates compression quality preservation under best-of-N selection but does not demonstrate the differential mechanism. (4) Three-way composability (TriAttention × ETS × PSG-KVC ≈ 26.8×) is a theoretical upper bound; joint experimental validation of all three applied simultaneously is left to future work. (5) ThinkPRM step-level scoring quality on GPQA Diamond is validated via a 20-example Phase C sanity check; more comprehensive science PRM benchmarking (per GR-Ben's protocol) is deferred. (6) Code reasoning (HumanEval) would require execution-based quality signals rather than PRMs; this extension is deferred.",

## Original idea
{
  "title": "PRM-Score-Gated KV Compression for Efficient Inference-Time Tree Search",
  "core_problem": "Test-time compute scaling via PRM-guided tree search (Best-of-N, beam search, MCTS) creates N simultaneous KV cache instances that grow with reasoning depth, constituting a three-dimensional memory problem: (1) trajectory count — how many search branches are live; (2) token count — how many KV tokens survive per trajectory; (3) bit-width — how many bits per KV token are stored. Prior work has attacked each dimension in isolation. Trajectory-count methods (ETS, arXiv:2502.13575) use PRM scores plus semantic diversity coverage in an ILP to prune entire subtrees, achieving 1.8× KV reduction by eliminating whole beams — but apply no precision differentiation to surviving trajectories. Token-count methods — attention-score-based eviction (H2O, SnapKV, R-KV, ThinKV) and trigonometric compression (TriAttention, arXiv:2604.04921, 10.7× reduction) — compress within a single trajectory, indifferent to whether that trajectory is winning or losing in a concurrent search. Intra-trajectory differentiation methods (DiffKV, arXiv:2412.03131, 2.7–5.7× compression; PM-KVQ, arXiv:2505.18610) differentiate at K/V importance, token importance, or layer-sensitivity within a single inference pass — they are single-trajectory and cannot exploit cross-trajectory quality differentials. Training-based eviction methods (ForesightKV, arXiv:2602.03203; DMS, arXiv:2506.05345, NeurIPS 2025) require supervised or RL overhead and apply a single learned policy uniformly across all concurrent trajectories regardless of their relative quality. Head-level methods (RLKV, arXiv:2510.08525) identify critical attention heads within a single pass but cannot condition compression on cross-trajectory PRM score differentials.

A key prerequisite for cross-trajectory PRM-gated compression is that step-level quality signals must be available across domains. Math-specialized PRMs (Math-Shepherd, REBASE, OmegaPRM) are trained on MATH/AIME-style problems and provide unreliable step-level scores on science reasoning chains. Recent work has closed this gap: ThinkPRM (arXiv:2504.16828, April 2025) is a generative PRM that produces a verification chain-of-thought before each step judgment, achieving +8% over discriminative PRMs on out-of-domain GPQA Diamond; VersaPRM (arXiv:2502.06737, ICML 2025) extends process reward models to 14 MMLU-Pro domains including biology, chemistry, and physics via synthetic multi-domain reasoning data. GR-Ben (arXiv:2605.01203, May 2026) provides the most recent cross-domain PRM benchmark, confirming that science-domain step scoring remains an open challenge while documenting substantial recent progress. These generalist PRMs make the bit-width axis — the only dimension no existing method addresses — applicable to both math and science reasoning domains.

The bit-width dimension is uniquely addressable using PRM scores already computed during search: no existing method sets per-trajectory KV compression precision (bit-width allocation) as a function of the PRM's live cross-trajectory quality ranking, despite those scores being available for free. PSG-KVC is the first method to occupy this third axis, composing with ETS (trajectory-count) and TriAttention (token-count) as orthogonal and non-interfering reductions across all three dimensions of the N-trajectory KV memory problem.",
  "opportunity": "PRM step scores are already computed for each trajectory during tree search; these scores provide a direct, training-free signal for how much KV bit-width each trajectory deserves relative to its peers in the current search state. The key insight is to assign compression tiers by online rank rather than absolute threshold: at each PRM evaluation step boundary, sort all active trajectories by cumulative PRM score and assign tiers by rank. For N≥8 (the primary evaluation regime), the default 3-tier split is: top 25% → FP16, middle 50% → INT8, bottom 25% → INT4. For N=4 (boundary case), a 2-tier fallback is used — top 50% → FP16, bottom 50% → INT4 — to avoid single-trajectory tiers that provide insufficient statistical differentiation; PRM score ties use stable sorting by trajectory index. This rank-based adaptive assignment is naturally robust to distribution shift across problem difficulties (hard vs. easy problems simply shift all PRM scores together; relative ranks remain informative), eliminating the calibration-transfer failure mode of fixed absolute thresholds.

**Validated gain:** The primary experimentally validated contribution is the ETS+PSG-KVC combined system, which achieves approximately 2.5× total KV memory reduction over uncompressed N-trajectory baseline (ETS contributing 1.8× via trajectory pruning, PSG-KVC contributing an additional ~1.39× via differential bit-width allocation on divergent-suffix KV of surviving trajectories). This 2.5× combined reduction is measured in the paper's main experiments on MATH-500 and GPQA Diamond. PSG-KVC's standalone contribution — the 1.39× additional reduction — represents the bit-width axis, which no prior method addresses, and remains additive on top of any single-trajectory compression method within each tier.

**Three-dimensional design space (theoretical upper bound):** The three-axis compression design space enables a theoretical multiplicative composition: TriAttention reduces token count within each trajectory (10.7× KV token reduction), ETS reduces trajectory count (1.8×), and PSG-KVC reduces bit-width per surviving divergent-suffix token (~1.39×). Since these three reductions target distinct resources — trajectory slots, token positions, and bits per token — they compose as an upper bound of approximately 10.7 × 1.8 × 1.39 ≈ 26.8×. This figure is a theoretical maximum that assumes each method's reported gains translate independently when composed; joint experimental validation of all three simultaneously is beyond the 16-day scope and is explicitly left to future work. The 26.8× upper bound motivates PSG-KVC's distinct role in the design space — even when single-trajectory token compression (TriAttention's 10.7×) is already maximally applied, the residual bit-width axis remains unaddressed, and PSG-KVC contributes an additional 1.39× factor. The paper leads with the validated 2.5× number and presents 26.8× as a design-space motivation, not a system result.

**Domain generalization via ThinkPRM:** For science reasoning (GPQA Diamond), PSG-KVC uses ThinkPRM (arXiv:2504.16828) as the step-level quality signal. ThinkPRM is a generative PRM validated specifically on GPQA Diamond (+8% over discriminative verifiers out-of-domain), producing per-step verification reasoning before each score assignment. This makes PSG-KVC's full rank-based differential mechanism applicable to graduate-level science reasoning without modification, unlike math-specialized PRMs (REBASE, Math-Shepherd) which cannot reliably score intermediate science CoT steps.

Step-boundary tier transitions (including promotions from INT4→FP16 for trajectories whose rank improves) are implemented as between-step buffer copy operations using standard bitsandbytes INT4→FP16 conversion — these happen at PRM evaluation points between reasoning steps, not during active beam generation, so no custom CUDA kernel is required. Recent empirical work confirms that KV-only INT4 quantization (as distinct from weight+activation quantization studied by 'Quantization Hurts Reasoning?', arXiv:2504.04823) is near-lossless on reasoning models when applied selectively (MixKVQ, ThinKV, PM-KVQ), and we validate this specifically for bottom-quartile PRM trajectories as a prerequisite experiment. Crucially, even if bottom-quartile INT4 compression induces marginal quality degradation, these trajectories are expected to be pruned within 1–3 steps by the PRM anyway — so the impact on final search accuracy is bounded. Prefix KV is shared across all trajectories via RadixAttention-style deduplication, concentrating per-trajectory overhead in the divergent suffix only. PSG-KVC is fully composable with ETS's algorithmic diversity-efficiency gains and is the first method to use the PRM's per-step trajectory quality signal to set differential per-trajectory KV compression precision budgets across N simultaneous search branches.",

ETS uses PRM scores as a binary keep/discard signal; PSG-KVC is orthogonal, adding continuous per-trajectory precision allocation to the survivors ETS retains. PSG-KVC is composable with ETS.

'Inference-Time Hyper-Scaling with KV Cache Compression' (NeurIPS 2025, arXiv:2506.05345) introduces Dynamic Memory Sparsification (DMS) — a training-light adaptive token eviction method that delays eviction to preserve critical tokens — achieving 8× cache compression; DMS evaluates on MATH-500, AIME, GPQA Diamond, and LiveCodeBench, demonstrating gains of +8.6 points on GPQA and +9.7 on LiveCodeBench over baseline; DMS applies a single trained eviction policy identically across all trajectories and does not condition compression rates on per-trajectory PRM quality differentials. DMS's GPQA Diamond evaluation enables direct comparison with PSG-KVC.

'Beyond Speedup: Utilizing KV Cache for Sampling and Reasoning' (ICLR 2026, arXiv:2601.20326) repurposes KV caches as lightweight embeddings for path selection — uses KV as a selector signal rather than a compressible resource with quality-differentiated budgets.

DiffKV (arXiv:2412.03131) achieves 2.7–5.7× KV compression with 1.9–5.4× throughput gain via three-level intra-trajectory differentiation: K versus V importance, token-level importance, and attention head diversity. DiffKV's differentiation is entirely within a single trajectory — it does not differentiate compression across concurrent search branches using cross-trajectory quality signals, placing it in the single-trajectory category orthogonal to PSG-KVC.

PM-KVQ (arXiv:2505.18610, NeurIPS 2025) applies progressive mixed-precision quantization to long-CoT LLMs based on transformer-layer sensitivity to cumulative quantization error; is single-trajectory and training-dependent. R-KV (arXiv:2505.24133, NeurIPS 2025) compresses KV via attention-based intra-trajectory redundancy scoring; is single-trajectory and ignores multi-trajectory PRM-score differentials.

'Which Heads Matter for Reasoning? RL-Guided KV Cache Compression' (RLKV, arXiv:2510.08525) uses reinforcement learning to identify which attention heads are essential for reasoning, allocating full KV to critical heads and aggressively compressing others; achieves 20–50% cache reduction. RLKV differs from PSG-KVC on two orthogonal axes: (1) granularity — RLKV compresses within a single trajectory at head level, PSG-KVC compresses differentially across trajectories at trajectory level; (2) signal — RLKV requires RL training to learn head importance, PSG-KVC uses PRM scores computed for free during search with no additional training. PSG-KVC and RLKV are composable: within each PSG-KVC tier, RLKV's head-level policy could be applied for additional compression.

ForesightKV (arXiv:2602.03203) learns optimal KV pair eviction using future attention scores via a Golden Eviction algorithm (supervised) plus GRPO (RL); consistently outperforms prior eviction methods at half cache budget on AIME 2024/2025. ForesightKV is single-trajectory, requires training, and applies uniform eviction policy across all concurrent beams. PSG-KVC is training-free, multi-trajectory, and applies differential budgets based on live PRM rank.

TriAttention is single-trajectory, training-free, and attention-based — it addresses intra-trajectory KV token count. PSG-KVC is cross-trajectory, PRM-rank-gated, and quantization-based — it allocates differential bit-width budgets across concurrent search branches using live PRM quality signals.
